purpose: Early, cheaper check for any edge in the S1 trade-flow idea using free historical trades, before the 60-day order-book collection for S1 completes. Not a substitute for S1.

data_source.time_unit: milliseconds before 2025-01-01, microseconds from 2025-01-01; detected per value (>= 1e14 means microseconds)
data_source.aggressor: is_buyer_maker=true means the seller was the aggressor (sell), false means buyer aggressor (buy)
data_source.missing_day_policy: fail closed: every UTC day in the loaded range must be present and checksum-verified
data_source.order_policy: fail closed if trade time decreases within a file or across consecutive files

window_utc.choice: fixed before any data in this window was examined; most recent 60 complete days old enough to be published, ending well before this spec was written

clock.time_base: exchange trade time (historical files have no local receive time); caveat: no capture latency is modeled beyond execution_delay_seconds
clock.bucket: 1-second buckets; bucket b holds trades with time in (b-1, b] seconds from range start
clock.grid: UTC 30-second grid aligned to the window start

features.signed_aggressor_qty_ratio_30s: (buy_aggressor_qty - sell_aggressor_qty) / (buy_aggressor_qty + sell_aggressor_qty) over trades in (t-30s, t]; requires >= 2 trades in the window
features.momentum_60s: last_price(t) / last_price(t-60s) - 1, where last_price(x) is the last trade at or before x
features.no_change: constant 0 score: predicts no move, never enters

decision_rule.rule: at grid time t, if flat and score(t) > threshold, buy; sell exactly horizon_seconds later; long or flat only, one position at a time, signals while in a position are ignored
decision_rule.configurations: each candidate threshold x each horizon = 12 configurations; this is the whole trial budget

execution_and_costs.fee_note: 0.10% per side (0.20% round trip), no verified lower fee tier
execution_and_costs.price_reference: last trade price at or before t + execution_delay_seconds (entry) and t + horizon + execution_delay_seconds (exit); both must be <= max_trade_age_seconds old, otherwise the signal is skipped (entry) or the exit uses the stale price anyway and is flagged (exit)
execution_and_costs.adverse_price_adjustment_breakdown: 1.0 bp half-spread (buy at the ask, sell at the bid) + 1.0 bp slippage; entry = ref * (1 + 2bp), exit = ref * (1 - 2bp)
execution_and_costs.caveat: No bid/ask or depth data in these files. Book side is approximated from the last trade plus a fixed half-spread and slippage. BTCUSDT spot's typical quoted spread is far below 1 bp, so this is meant to be conservative for small size, but it is an assumption, not a measurement. Queueing, partial fills and size beyond top-of-book are not modeled.

chronological_split.segments: train [start, validation_start), validation [validation_start, test_start), test [test_start, end)
chronological_split.purge_rule: an entry at t is allowed only if t + horizon + execution_delay_seconds <= segment_end - purge (purge applies at the train/validation and validation/test boundaries and at window end)
chronological_split.embargo_rule: the first eligible prediction in validation and test is at segment_start + embargo; train starts after warmup
chronological_split.train_role: in-sample diagnostics only; the rules are fixed and nothing is fitted

selection.metric: mean net return per trade after costs
selection.tie_break: more validation trades, then lower threshold, then shorter horizon
selection.if_no_configuration_has_min_trades: nothing is selected; verdict fail; test is not run
selection.report_all_configurations: all 12 validation results are reported (multiple-comparison caveat)

test_evaluation.evaluates: the single validation-selected configuration plus baselines on the test segment
test_evaluation.enforcement: runner refuses a second test run (exclusive marker file next to the data); changing anything after seeing test results spends the test set and must be reported

baselines.no_change: constant 0 score never exceeds a positive threshold: 0 trades, 0 return (economically identical to no_trade)
baselines.always_long_same_horizon: score = +inf at every eligible grid time, same horizon, same costs and non-overlap rule as the selected configuration
baselines.buy_and_hold: one round trip from the first to the last eligible time of the segment, same costs

all_required: test mean net return per trade > 0
test mean net return per trade > always_long_same_horizon mean net return on test
pass_criteria.otherwise: fail: stop or change the hypothesis in a new spec version; no tuning on test
pass_criteria.meaning_of_pass: evidence worth paying for the S1 order-book experiment's attention; not a profitability claim for live trading given the price-approximation caveat
